description.narrative: Under this project, the focus is on the Kukus (people of Kuku tribe) and the Banyara. The Kuku are a large ethnic group in the southern region of Sudan. They belong to a cultural and linguistic group called the Eastern Nilotes. The history of Banyala istraced to the wars of Buganda against Bunyoro before 1900. They are a result of intermarriages between Banyoro and Baganda supported by the British Empire. The kuku and Banyara are agricultural people. They had no kingship. In the 2014 population census in Uganda the Kuku were (46497) and above 8300 in only Kayunga district. Basing on their way of life, life of these people is becoming hard because of the differences in socio-cultural practices, history and backgrounds, minorities have to grapple with theissue of identity, insecurity, discriminatory denial and this is the gist of this project. The minority community in a society may remain deprived of the benefit of opportunities of development as a result of discrimination. They cannot be employed, children go to poor schools, poor or less health services, no community engagement and inferiority complex among them, Because of the difference in identity, the minority community develops the perception of the sense of inequity. STAY IN SCHOOL INITIATIVE aims at fighting for the rights of ethnic minority groups with help of this proposed project which is aiming at providing sustainable vocational skills, Mentoring, Sensitizing, and empowering 20 youths from ethnic minority families in Busaana Town council.The project is aiming to directly benefit 20 youths wherethey will be skilled in hairdressing and tailoring activities for the period of one year. These beneficiaries will directly benefitin such a way of being employed, establishing their own businesses,gaining life skills and many others.

participating-org.narrative:
Stay In School Initiative is a nonprofit civil society organization that was established and registered in 2019 with the governmentof Uganda. It was founded by a team of five (5) experienced and competent youths motivated by the love of minority communities and the dire need for concerted efforts to fight poverty, illiteracy and diseases in Uganda. It was founded by; Lutakome Ivan, Bwowe Joseph, Mwogeza Jonah, Wanguja Yusuf and Iga Alex. The organization was initiated as a small mutual support group offive individuals within Kampala who began reaching out to other needy and unprivileged families in Kayunga district voluntarily as need arose using thelocal resources within their families and communities. We started offering financial support and scholastic materials to over twenty (20) school going children from less privileged families towards their education and this number has since then increased. Ssezibwa COU Primary school in Kayunga Sub County was the first school we partnered with so that thekids on our Education sponsorship programme do get good Education. In 2019, we discovered that a lot of children from the ethnic minority families were dropping from school because of segregation and due to some cultural beliefs. Stay IN School Initiative has been very critical in fighting school dropouts in Kayunga District, towards this cause, for the past three years, the organization has provided scholastic materials, uniforms,lunch and part of school fees to orphaned pupils as well as sensitizationagainst discrimination and cultural beliefs in a struggle of lessening the percentage of school dropout as well as increasing the Primary Leaving Examination performance at the district level.
As Stay In School, we have been able to provide scholasticmaterials to pupils from the less privileged families among the ethnicminority groups in the society. This has greatly empowered them and changed their attitude towards Education and this has led to a reduced level of school dropouts during the CORONA virus.
For the past years, Stay in School initiative has initiated a saving scheme for the parents and guardians benefiting from the organisation. During this course, the organisation sensitized the parents and guardians on the benefits of saving and educating their children and this has enabled them sending their children to school with food, scholastic materials and school fees.
In 2021, in collaboration with KANGO with support from GIZ, stay in school initiative managed to reach hundreds of householdsaiming at sensitizing them about control and prevention of COVID-19. Under this project, over 408 households were visited and their thoughts about covid19changed and people started maintaining the SOPs.
Institutional objectives: What are the principalchanges the organisation seeks to achieve over the long term? i. To contribute towards community development through sensitizing the locals about the value of an educated child, education and also their rights through arranging meetings, seminars and conferences. ii. To provide education through financial, material and technical support to existing and new public and private educational institutions and libraries. iii. To increase collaboration plans with other health organisations to provide public health awareness campaigns to the people of Kayunga District. iv. To spot and nurture fresh talents through mentoring youths over sports, community services, and hands-on skills training to help them grow into responsible citizens.
